search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; measurement-validity/benchmark-design; exact sequential paired-binary/task-finalization inference under optional stopping

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: E-values for k-Sample Tests with Exponential Families
sources_checked_or_revisited.authors: Yunda Hao, Peter Grünwald, Tyron Lardy, Long Long, Reuben Adams
sources_checked_or_revisited.action: Verified the Bernoulli k=2 conditional e-variable construction. Conditional on the pair sum Z, concordant outcomes contribute factor 1; discordant outcomes contribute a conditional likelihood-ratio e-variable. The paper states that multiplying block e-variables gives an anytime-valid test under optional stopping and notes the Bernoulli connection to Wald's sequential two-proportion test.

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: Anytime validity is free: inducing sequential tests
sources_checked_or_revisited.authors: Nick W. Koning, Sam van Meer
sources_checked_or_revisited.action: Verified that any valid terminal test can be induced backward into an anytime-valid sequential test that matches the terminal test at the planned horizon; verified the composite-null extension via pointwise tests/running infimum and optional-continuation results.

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: The McNemar test for binary matched-pairs data: mid-p and asymptotic are better than exact conditional
sources_checked_or_revisited.authors: Morten W. Fagerland, Stian Lydersen, Petter Laake
sources_checked_or_revisited.action: Rechecked the matched-pair model and exact conditional McNemar structure: for i.i.d. bivariate Bernoulli pairs, marginal homogeneity is equivalent to equality of the two discordant-cell probabilities, and the exact conditional test reduces to a binomial split among discordant pairs.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: For each completed task, emit exactly one paired binary task outcome (A_t,B_t) in {0,1}^2 after all within-task rollout collection/aggregation is finished. Let candidate-win discordance be (1,0), loss discordance be (0,1), and concordances be (0,0)/(1,1). Choose q_t predictably from past completed tasks with q_t in [1/2,1]. Use per-task factor e_t=1 for concordance, e_t=2 q_t for a candidate-win discordance, and e_t=2(1-q_t) for a candidate-loss discordance. Under the one-sided conditional null P((1,0)|discordant,F_{t-1}) <= 1/2, E[e_t|F_{t-1}] <= 1, so the product is an exact nonnegative supermartingale/e-process. Reject at product >=1/alpha. A fixed q corresponds to the Bernoulli conditional-likelihood-ratio construction; predictable q_t or a mixture can adapt to unknown effect size without invalidating optional stopping.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.derivation: For a discordant task with null win probability p_t<=1/2, conditional expected factor is 2[p_t q_t+(1-p_t)(1-q_t)] = 2[(1-q_t)+p_t(2q_t-1)] <=1 because q_t>=1/2. Concordant tasks have factor 1. Therefore variable tie/discordance rates and data-dependent stopping across completed tasks do not affect Type-I validity as long as the conditional discordant-sign null holds.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Hao et al. verify the k=2 Bernoulli conditional e-variable and that concordant outcomes have factor 1; they also state blockwise multiplication yields anytime-valid optional-stopping tests. Exact McNemar conditions identify the discordant sign split as the relevant matched-pair null statistic. The one-sided composite-null inequality above is a direct extension/derivation from these ingredients.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: This is exact for the induced task-level paired outcome process under a conditional per-task no-better/symmetry null. It does not by itself test an average-only null that allows some tasks to favor the candidate conditional on the past. It also does not justify treating multiple correlated rollouts inside a task as independent discordant pairs.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Need power/growth comparison among fixed-q, plug-in, and mixture alternatives at only 10-50 independent tasks, especially when discordance is sparse.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Allow a task to use a variable and outcome-adaptive number of internally correlated rollouts, but freeze a symmetric task-finalization rule before evaluation and feed only the final paired task outcome to the outer sequential test. The internal adaptive process may be arbitrarily complicated from the outer test's perspective; what matters is the induced distribution of the final task pair. Thus within-task optional stopping is not automatically a statistical violation, but it becomes part of the estimand/evaluation policy.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: The conditional e-variable is defined on a completed block, and Safe Testing-style composition from the prior checkpoint only needs block-level conditional validity. The McNemar/e-process derivation above depends only on the final pair's discordant-sign probability given prior completed tasks, not on rollout-level independence.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: If the stopping/aggregation rule differs between systems, uses asymmetric access to outcomes, or is changed after seeing partial results, equality of underlying single-rollout performance need not imply equality/symmetry of the induced final task outcomes. The resulting test is then valid only for the induced evaluation policy, not automatically for a latent per-rollout capability claim.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Need concrete symmetric finalization policies for common agent settings (fixed compute budget, first-success-with-equal-budget, majority/mean threshold, verifier-gated stopping) and adversarial examples showing when seemingly symmetric adaptive stopping still changes the target.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: When a maximum number N of independent task pairs is planned and terminal exact McNemar (or another exact paired test) is the desired endpoint, induce an anytime-valid sequential test backward from that terminal test by taking its null conditional rejection probability given the current filtration. This preserves the exact terminal test at N instead of paying the usual power gap of a forward-designed generic e-process.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Koning and van Meer prove that any valid terminal test can be sequentialized into an anytime-valid process that equals the original test at the terminal horizon, and extend the construction to composite nulls by inducing pointwise tests and taking the running infimum. Exact McNemar provides a valid finite-sample terminal matched-pair test under its assumptions.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: The construction requires the conditional expectation under the relevant null family to be computable or approximated safely. Exact McNemar's nuisance/conditioning structure and heterogeneous/adaptively selected tasks may make this nontrivial. A Monte Carlo approximation must itself preserve validity; a naive approximate conditional rejection probability is not automatically safe.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Derive a computationally explicit recursion for terminal exact McNemar under a fixed N and compare its early stopping behavior with the forward conditional e-process.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Report discordance rate as a first-class resolution diagnostic for paired binary agent evaluation. In the conditional McNemar e-process, concordant tasks contribute exactly no evidence, so nominal task count can substantially overstate information. For a correctly specified fixed alternative q, expected log growth per discordant task is KL(Bern(q)||Bern(1/2)); expected log growth per total task is approximately r times this quantity where r is the discordance probability.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: These are expected-log-growth approximations, not guaranteed stopping times or power calculations. They assume the chosen alternative q matches the true conditional win probability among discordances and a stable discordance rate.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Need exact/simulated stopping distributions and unresolved rates under mixtures, sparse discordance, and heterogeneous task strata.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Variable/adaptive within-task rollout counts necessarily invalidate an outer anytime-valid task-level test.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected as too broad. If each completed task is collapsed to one final paired outcome and the null is formulated for that induced task-level outcome, the outer e-process can be exact without rollout-level independence. The unresolved issue is estimand preservation: adaptive finalization changes what is being tested unless the policy is frozen and interpreted explicitly.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Exact McNemar can safely treat every correlated rollout pair inside one task as an independent matched pair.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Classical exact McNemar assumes mutually independent matched pairs (or an equivalent conditional structure). Correlated rollout pairs within a task cause pseudo-replication. One task should remain one outer unit unless stronger within-task assumptions/randomization justify more evidence.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: McNemar's marginal-homogeneity null across the realized sample is interchangeable with the conditional per-task no-better null used by the simple e-process.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. The simple multiplicative factor is exact under the stronger conditional null p_t<=1/2 among discordances for every completed task given the past. An average-only weak null can allow local positive conditional effects and needs a weak-null CS/e-process such as the paired bounded-score route from the prior checkpoint.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Inducing an anytime-valid terminal McNemar test makes finite-horizon sequentialization computationally free as well as statistically free.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. The 2026 theorem removes the terminal power penalty in principle, but computing conditional rejection probabilities for a composite/conditioned matched-pair test can still be difficult.

design_implications.binary_task_default: one task -> one finalized paired binary outcome -> exact discordance-sign e-process; never count internal rollouts as independent tasks
design_implications.adaptive_internal_sampling: allowed only as part of a frozen task-finalization policy; interpret inference as applying to that induced policy
design_implications.conditional_null_route: use sequential McNemar/sign e-process when a per-task conditional no-better/symmetry null is scientifically acceptable
design_implications.weak_average_null_route: use paired bounded-score average-conditional-mean CS/e-process when only average performance is the target
design_implications.known_horizon_route: consider induced anytime-valid terminal exact test to retain terminal fixed-N power
design_implications.resolution_reporting: report discordant-task count/rate alongside total tasks and unresolved status

frontier_queue.action: Derive and simulate mixture/predictable-q sequential McNemar e-processes at N=10,20,30,50 tasks across discordance rates 0.1-0.8 and conditional win probabilities 0.55-0.9; report Type-I, stopping probability, median stopping time and unresolved rate.

Construct an explicit backward recursion for an induced anytime-valid exact McNemar terminal test at fixed maximum N, including composite-null conditioning, and compare terminal/early power with the forward e-process.

Design symmetric within-task adaptive rollout finalization policies and prove which latent null they preserve; build counterexamples where asymmetric or model-specific stopping creates task-level bias despite equal single-rollout marginals.
Extend the exact task-finalized route from binary outcomes to bounded reward differences while distinguishing conditional per-task nulls from weak average nulls.
Connect task-population sampling/generalization to the paired sequential test so that optional stopping validity on realized tasks is not confused with external benchmark-population generalization.

early_termination_avoidance: This run found an exact sequential McNemar-style e-process that absorbs arbitrary within-task rollout dependence by keeping one completed task as one outer paired observation, but it also identified a stricter null/estimand boundary and a finite-horizon induced-test route that still needs computation and power characterization. The frontier therefore remains materially nonempty.
exact_next_action: Numerically compare fixed-q, predictable plug-in and mixture sequential McNemar e-processes at 10-50 tasks under varying discordance rates, then derive the backward induced terminal-McNemar recursion for a known task horizon.
